topics.SPA: Spatial: nets, cubes, views and routes

questions.stem:
Nina says: 'The shop has run out of chocolate ice cream, so I won't have any dessert today.'
What has Nina assumed?

options.A: The shop will get more ice cream tomorrow.
options.B: Chocolate ice cream is the only dessert she will have.

questions.explanation: She could have a different dessert. Her conclusion only works if chocolate ice cream is the only choice.

distractors.A: not about today
distractors.C: maybe, but her conclusion depends on it being the only dessert

questions.stem:
Grace says: 'Our school should plant more trees in the playground. It would give us more shade on hot days.'
Which statement best supports Grace's argument?

options.A: On hot days, most of the playground is in full sun and there is nowhere cool to sit.
options.C: Grace's favourite tree is the jacaranda.
options.D: The school has a big library.

questions.explanation: Grace's reason is shade. Showing that the playground has almost no shade now makes her point stronger.

distractors.C: about her opinion, not the reason

questions.stem:
A cat is lighter than a dog. A rabbit is lighter than a cat. A horse is heavier than a dog.
Which animal is the lightest?
questions.explanation: Order from heaviest: horse, dog, cat, rabbit. The rabbit is the lightest.

distractors.A: the rabbit is lighter than the cat
distractors.C: the dog is heavier than the cat

questions.stem:
Pip is taller than Kim. Kim is taller than Sol.
Which statement CANNOT be true?

options.A: Pip is the tallest of the three.
options.B: Sol is the shortest of the three.

questions.explanation: The order is Pip, then Kim, then Sol. Sol is the shortest, so Sol can't be taller than Pip.

distractors.A: this must be true

questions.stem:
Coach Ali says: 'If we practise passing every training session, we will score more goals.'
Which statement, if true, best supports the coach?

options.A: Our team has new shirts this season.
options.B: The other teams also train twice a week.
options.C: Last season, most of our goals came straight after a good pass.
options.D: Passing drills are easy to set up.

questions.explanation: If good passes usually lead to goals, getting better at passing should lead to more goals.

distractors.A: not connected
distractors.D: about how easy, not whether it works

questions.stem: A movie is 1 hour 45 minutes long. It finishes at 4:30 pm. What time did it start?
questions.explanation: Count back 1 hour from 4:30 pm: 3:30 pm. Then 45 more minutes back: 2:45 pm.

distractors.A: counted back only 1 hour 15 minutes
distractors.C: added instead of counting back

questions.stem:
Four friends ran a race.
• Sana finished straight after Max.
• Tom did not come first.
• Ella did not come last.
• Tom finished before Max.
Who came last?
questions.explanation: Max and Sana finish one after the other, and Tom is before Max, so Tom, Max, Sana are in that order. Tom isn't first, so Ella is first. Order: Ella, Tom, Max, Sana.

distractors.A: check every clue against your order
distractors.B: check every clue against your order
distractors.C: check every clue against your order

questions.stem:
The school bus is usually on time, but this morning it was 20 minutes late.
Which statement best explains this?

options.A: A fallen tree blocked the main road, so the bus had to go a longer way.
options.B: The bus driver's name is Mr Rossi.
options.D: Some students like sitting at the back.

questions.explanation: A blocked road forcing a longer route would make the bus late.

distractors.C: not connected

questions.stem:
Rule: Children can join the swimming squad only if they can swim 50 metres without stopping.
Tara: 'Lucas is in the squad, so he can swim 50 metres without stopping.'
Jack: 'Zoe can swim 50 metres without stopping, so she is in the squad.'
If the rule is followed, whose reasoning is correct?
questions.explanation: Tara ✓: everyone in the squad must be able to swim 50 metres. Jack ✗: Zoe can swim 50 metres, but she may not have joined the squad.

distractors.B: being able to swim 50 m doesn't mean she joined
distractors.C: Zoe might not have joined

questions.stem:
Every time Rory wears his lucky socks, it rains. So Rory's socks make it rain.
What is the mistake in this reasoning?

options.C: Two things happening together doesn't mean one causes the other.
options.D: Socks can get wet in the rain.

questions.explanation: Socks can't change the weather. It is just a coincidence (or Rory notices more when he wears them).

distractors.A: advice, not the mistake

questions.stem:
Jess asked three friends which movie they liked best, and all three chose the same movie. Jess says: 'Everyone in Australia likes that movie best.'
What is wrong with Jess's thinking?

options.A: The movie might be very long.
options.B: Three friends are far too few to tell what everyone in Australia thinks.

questions.explanation: Asking only three people, who are friends and may like the same things, can't show what millions of people think.

distractors.A: not about the reasoning
distractors.C: we don't know that, and it doesn't matter

questions.stem:
Owen says: 'We should get a robot vacuum cleaner. Then our floors will always be clean.'
Which statement, if true, most weakens Owen's argument?

options.A: Robot vacuums can't go up stairs or clean under very low furniture, and most of our house is stairs and rugs.
options.B: Robot vacuums come in different colours.
options.C: Owen's friend has a robot vacuum.
options.D: Vacuum cleaners were invented a long time ago.

questions.explanation: If the robot can't reach most of the house, the floors won't 'always be clean'.

distractors.C: doesn't say whether it works

questions.stem: I am a number between 40 and 70. I am in the 3 times table and the 5 times table, and I am even. What number am I?
questions.explanation: Numbers between 40 and 70 in both the 3 and 5 times tables: 45 and 60. Only 60 is even.

distractors.A: it is odd
distractors.C: not in the 3 times table

questions.explanation: Count: 7, 12, 17… Each new pattern adds 5 matchsticks. Pattern 15 = 7 + 14 × 5 = 77.

questions.skill: Gears: direction and number of turns
questions.stem: Gear A turns once clockwise. Which way does gear C turn, and how many times?
questions.explanation: Touching gears turn in opposite directions: A clockwise, B anticlockwise, C clockwise. The teeth pass one at a time, so one turn of A (16 teeth) moves 16 teeth of every gear. Gear C has 8 teeth, so it turns 16 ÷ 8 = 2 times. (The gears in between don't change this.)

distractors.A: each gear turns the opposite way to the one it touches: count the steps
distractors.C: a smaller gear turns more times
distractors.D: turns the wrong way and divided the wrong way round

questions.stem:
Most of the dogs at the park are on a lead.
Ivy: 'That dog at the park must be on a lead.'
Jai: 'If I pick any dog at the park, it is likely to be on a lead.'
If the information is true, whose reasoning is correct?
questions.explanation: Jai ✓: if most dogs are on a lead, any one dog is likely to be. Ivy ✗: 'most' isn't 'all', so that dog might not be.

distractors.A: 'most' doesn't mean 'all'
distractors.C: Jai's 'likely' is justified

distractors.A: Nia also needed to write a review
distractors.C: Oz's reasoning works

questions.stem:
On a farm there are some chickens and some cows. Altogether there are 12 heads and 34 legs.
How many cows are there?
questions.explanation: If all 12 were chickens, there would be 24 legs. There are 10 extra legs, and each cow adds 2 extra legs, so there are 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cows (and 7 chickens). Check: 7 × 2 + 5 × 4 = 34 ✓.

distractors.A: that is the number of chickens

questions.stem:
Someone left the gate open. Exactly one of these three children is lying.
Ivy: 'It was Kit.'
Jay: 'It wasn't me.'
Kit: 'It was Jay.'
Who left the gate open?
questions.explanation: Ivy and Kit blame different people, so they can't both be telling the truth: one of them is the liar. That means Jay is telling the truth, so it wasn't Jay, and Kit's statement is the lie. Ivy is right: it was Kit.

distractors.A: then Ivy and Kit would both be lying
distractors.B: then Jay's statement would be a lie as well as Ivy's
distractors.C: only one person fits exactly one lie

questions.stem:
At a museum, children under 12 get in free. On Sundays, everyone gets a free badge.
Amir: 'I am 10, so I got in free.'
Bella: 'Carlos got a free badge, so it must be Sunday.'
If the information is true, whose reasoning is correct?
questions.explanation: Amir ✓: he is under 12, so he gets in free. Bella ✗: badges are given on Sundays, but they might also be given at other times; the rule doesn't say ONLY on Sundays.

distractors.A: badges might be given on other days too
distractors.B: Bella's conclusion doesn't have to be true

questions.stem:
All the red books in the library are on the top shelf. Some of the books on the top shelf are about animals.
Kip: 'So some of the red books are about animals.'
Lou: 'So a book on the bottom shelf can't be red.'
If the information is true, whose reasoning is correct?
questions.explanation: Lou ✓: every red book is on the top shelf, so a bottom-shelf book isn't red. Kip ✗: the animal books on the top shelf might all be other colours.

distractors.A: the animal books might not be red
distractors.C: Kip's conclusion doesn't have to be true

questions.stem:
Every Friday, the school canteen sells pizza. Today the canteen sold pizza.
Ray: 'So today must be Friday.'
Sia: 'If tomorrow is Friday, the canteen will sell pizza tomorrow.'
If the information is true, whose reasoning is correct?
questions.explanation: Sia ✓: the canteen sells pizza every Friday. Ray ✗: it might sell pizza on other days too; the rule doesn't say ONLY on Fridays.

distractors.B: pizza might be sold on other days too
distractors.C: Ray's conclusion doesn't have to be true

questions.stem: In a bike shed there are 11 bicycles and tricycles. Altogether they have 26 wheels. How many tricycles are there?
questions.explanation: If all 11 were bicycles, there would be 22 wheels. Each tricycle adds 1 extra wheel, and there are 26 − 22 = 4 extra, so 4 tricycles (and 7 bicycles).

distractors.A: that is the number of bicycles
distractors.C: one tricycle too many (27 wheels)
